neighbours.label: a deictic time expression anchored to the present (ago, last night, today, tomorrow, yesterday) in the middle of a sentence
fire: My uncle sold his old truck to a neighbour about two months ago.
We heard a loud crash in the street last night around eleven.
Nobody can promise that tomorrow will bring better weather.
The doctor told me that a few years ago this test did not exist.
Honestly, I felt much calmer today than I did all week.
She called her mother yesterday to wish her a happy birthday.
The shop that opened a decade ago is still run by the same family.
Something strange happened at the station last night after the storm.
quiet: My uncle sold his old truck to a neighbour who needed it for work.
We heard a loud crash in the street around eleven during the storm.
Nobody can promise that the new season will bring better weather.
The doctor told me that in earlier decades this test did not exist.
Honestly, I felt much calmer after the meeting than before it.
She called her mother on her birthday to wish her well.
The shop that opened in 1990 is still run by the same family.
Something strange happened at the station after the storm in April.
